claims.text: W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 and NbMoTaW are refractory high-entropy alloys belonging to a Group IV-V transition-metal alloy family.
Interstitial O, N, and C impurities in these powders arise from raw materials and the processing atmosphere.
PBF-LB/M can form W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 in situ from a mixture of elemental powders with substantially complete fusion.
Optimized PBF-LB/M can produce material with relative density greater than 99.8%.
PBF-LB/M of W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 can produce a single BCC phase.
PBF-LB/M produces a dendritic or cellular microstructure whose morphology can be controlled to some extent through process parameters.
SLM using a linear energy density of at least 2.83 J/mm enables formation of a single-BCC NbMoTaW alloy.
Following additive manufacturing with high-temperature annealing enables retention of high-temperature structural integrity.
High-temperature annealing homogenizes the additively manufactured microstructure.
Annealing reduces the concentration or detrimental effects of O, N, and C interstitial impurities in the additively manufactured alloys.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the single-phase BCC structure.
Rapid solidification during additive manufacturing causes formation of a refined microstructure.
A homogeneous, refined, single-phase BCC state with minimized interstitial content is the optimal microstructure for mechanical performance.
Ordered interstitial complexes pin dislocations and reduce ductility.
Minimizing the clustering of interstitials into ordered complexes mitigates brittleness.
The proposed processing route enhances elevated-temperature strength, ductility, creep resistance, and structural integrity.
The proposed route outperforms conventionally processed or unannealed additively manufactured refractory HEAs.
Refractory HEAs based on W, Mo, Ta, or Nb are of interest for high-temperature aerospace and chemical-industry applications.
The high melting points and segregation tendency of refractory HEAs make conventional metallurgical processing challenging.
Single-phase BCC formation is thermodynamically favorable throughout the stated W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V-Hf-Zr alloy family.

contradictions.description: The alloy family is labeled as Group IV-V, but the listed elements W and Mo are Group VI transition metals.
